title: December User Group - Writing code got easier. Shipping it feels harder.
thumbnailDescription: Writing code got easier. Shipping it feels harder. With Matt Wicks at Sydney .NET User Group on 16 December
abstract: Writing code got easier. Shipping it feels harder. Matt Wicks explores why AI can speed up development while leaving teams with bigger changes, review queues, and harder rollbacks. You'll leave knowing whether your team is shipping faster or just breaking things faster, and what to change when you get back to work.
description:
**Writing code got easier. Shipping it feels harder.**

AI made me faster. It's made most teams faster. The research says it's also made them less stable: bigger changes, smaller teams, and review queues that can't keep up.

By day I build enterprise apps for large clients. On the side I experiment, because the tools seem to change every couple of days. My latest experiment was an online store for my wife, in a stack I'd never touched, with AI writing most of it. Getting it working was the easy part. Keeping it safe to change is where it got hard, and teams shipping mostly AI-written code are hitting the same wall. When code is cheap, review, rollback and knowing how the system works become the real work.

You'll leave knowing whether your team is shipping faster or just breaking things faster, and what to change when you get back to work.
